items.title: FedDOSE: Federated Learning Framework Decomposing Site Effects for Modeling Brain Dynamic Functional Connectivity
items.abstract: Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging ( fMRI ) data are often pooled into collaborative multi-site consortia, as deep learning models for analyses require large datasets to generalize well. While Federated Learning (FL) offers a privacy-preserving paradigm for collaborative training, standard approaches continue to struggle with statistical heterogeneity. In particular, site differences pose a key challenge in multi-site data settings. Additionally, existing FL approaches for fMRI rely on static Functional Connectivity ( FC), omitting dynamic information in brain networks. To address this, we propose FedDOSE, a novel framework that explicitly decomposes site differences for analysis of dynamic FC (dFC). FedDOSE introduces a Modularity-Guided Tucker Decomposition block to encode high-dimensional dFC tensors and capture modular-level spatio-temporal patterns efficiently. Class-specific prototypes are generated across all sites and subsequently aligned at the global level by using a combination of Optimal Transport (OT) barycenter formulation and Procrustes analysis. Extensive experiments for diagnosing Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and Attention-Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD) on three multi-site resting-state fMRI datasets: ABIDE-I, ABIDE-II, and ADHD-200, demonstrate that FedDOSE outperforms state-of-the-art methods in ASD and ADHD detection. Our results highlight its effectiveness in learning robust representations from multi-site datasets for reliable analysis.

items.llm_tldr_en: FedDOSE decomposes site effects in federated learning to model brain dynamic functional connectivity from fMRI, addressing statistical heterogeneity while preserving dynamic brain-network information.
items.llm_tldr_cn: 多中心fMRI数据分析常面临站点差异和动态脑网络信息缺失的问题，现有联邦学习方法仅建模静态功能连接。该文提出FedDOSE框架，显式分解站点效应，并在联邦学习中建模动态功能连接(dFC)，在保护隐私的同时提升了多站点fMRI建模的泛化性与脑网络动态表征能力。该工作为神经影像的多中心协作研究提供了新方法。
